character: 250 km linking Alpe d'Huez, Vaujany, Oz-en-Oisans, and Auris. Home of the Sarenne — 16 km black run, longest in Europe.
description: 250km of linked pistes, 63 lifts, connecting Alpe d'Huez, Oz-en-Oisans, Vaujany, and Auris-en-Oisans. The domain sits on a massive south-facing plateau above the Romanche valley in the Oisans massif. Known for: the Sarenne run (16km black — Europe's longest single run), 300 days of sunshine per year, the Pic Blanc summit (3,330m), and the 21-turn 'Pas de la Confusion' off-piste route in the Sarenne valley. Sunny, snow-sure due to high altitude (Alpe d'Huez village at 1,860m).
name: Grand Domaine (Alpe d'Huez)

lift_pass_pricing.note: Alpe d'Huez only pass cheaper. Oz/Vaujany/Auris local passes available. Glacier access included.

suitability.beginners: Good — Alpe d'Huez village has a dedicated beginner area at the snow front. Oz 3300 and Vaujany have gentle greens. The Sarenne from mid-station down is a gentle blue that beginners can ski.
suitability.intermediates: Excellent — the south-facing plateau gives endless blue/red combinations. The run from Signal de l'Homme (2,800m) back to Alpe d'Huez is a classic 6km red/blue cruiser. Vaujany's return run through the forest.
suitability.advanced: Very good — the 21 black runs including the famous Sarenne (16km from 3,300m to 1,500m). The steep off-piste in the Sarenne couloirs. The Combe Charbonnière area.

signature_runs.name: Sarenne
signature_runs.description: Europe's longest single run — 16km from Pic Blanc (3,330m) to the Sarenne valley. A true classic. Blue alternative from mid-station.
